evidence.note: Early architecture decision explicitly names the shared substrate as prerequisites: SQLite (WAL) shared store for stable ids + dense seq, and a TCP broadcast hub with a DB-polling fallback for cross-node fan-out. Lays out a layered file plan (db.py → core.py → broadcast.py → app.py → static SPA → start.sh), i.e. foundations before dependents.
Build order is dependency-correct: DB schema first, then core helpers, then broadcast transport, then the full REST API, and only afterward the SPA — API built and verified before UI.

Verification followed the same dependency ladder each with an implicit done-check actually executed: health across 3 nodes → register/login → workspace read → message post → cross-node propagation → IRC → confirming dense seq (1,2) shared across HTTP+IRC writers.

The highest-risk cross-cutting invariants were isolated as their own checks: WS subscribe/head_seq, resume-across-nodes replay, and fan-out survival with the broadcast hub killed (fallback poller within 5s) — the load-bearing resilience milestones treated distinctly.

Plan revised as build revealed new dependencies: recognizing IRC-on-single-node fails under node kill, redesigned start.sh so all nodes race for the IRC port and tested takeover; supervisor/process-supervision treated as a first-class element rather than bolted on.
Course-correction milestone: discovered duplicate WS frames (hub + poller), paused to fix dedup by (channel_id, seq), then re-ran the substrate check — foundation stabilized before moving on.

reasoning: The agent clearly exceeds anchor 5: it produced a sensible, dependency-correct ordered breakdown, recognized the critical shared substrate (dense per-channel seq store, fan-out transport) at the very start, and sequenced foundations before dependents (DB/seq → WS/IRC/resilience; API → SPA). It reaches into anchor 8 territory by making dependencies visible, treating start.sh/supervision as a first-class concern it iterated on, isolating the highest-risk invariants (dense seq across HTTP+IRC, replay-on-reconnect, fan-out survival) as their own verified checks, and revising the design (IRC-on-all-nodes, dedup) as new dependencies surfaced. It falls short of a full 8/10 because the milestones live in prose 'Plan:' fields with executed rather than pre-declared acceptance criteria — no explicit milestone hierarchy — so it lands at 7.
